<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par58 />and with ''Mappiq'', since the {{GHGheb|text=ה}} is consonantal; but the weakening to {{GHGheb|text=־ָה}} is also found, see below, g.

{{GHGmargin-letter|58|e}}
'''3.''' The ''variety'' of the suffix-forms is occasioned chiefly by the fact that they are modified differently according to the form and tense of the verb to which they are attached. For almost every suffix three forms may be distinguished:

(''a'') One beginning with a consonant, as {{GHGheb|text=־֫נִי}}, {{GHGheb|text=־֫הוּ}}, {{GHGheb|text=ו}} (only after ''î''), {{GHGheb|text=־֫נוּ}}, {{GHGheb|text=ם (הֶם)}}, &c. These are attached to verbal forms which end with a vowel, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=יִקְטְל֫וּנִי}}; {{GHGheb|text=קְטַלְתִּ֫יהוּ}}, for which by absorption of the {{GHGheb|text=ה}} we also get {{GHGheb|text=קְטַלְתִּיו}}, pronounced ''q<sup>e</sup>ṭaltîu''; cf. {{GHGpar|8|m}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|58|f}}
(''b'') A second and third with what are called ''connecting vowels''<ref>We have kept the term ''connecting'' vowel, although it is rather a superficial description, and moreover these vowels are of various origin. The connective ''a'' is most probably the remains of the old verbal termination, like the ''i'' in the 2nd pers. {{GHGterm|fem.}} sing. {{GHGheb|text=קְטַלְתִּ֫יהוּ}}. Observe e.g. the Hebrew form ''q<sup>e</sup>ṭāl-ani'' in connexion with the Arabic ''qatala-ni'', contrasted with Hebrew ''q<sup>e</sup>ṭālat-ni'' and Arabic ''qatalat-ni''. König accordingly prefers the expression ‘vocalic ending of the stem’, instead of ‘connecting syllable’. The connective ''ē'', aŒ¬, as Prätorius ({{GHGcite|title={{abbr|ZDMG.|Zeitschrift der deutschen morgenländischen Gesellschaft, Lpz. 1846 ff., since 1903 ed. by A. Fischer.}}}} 55, 267 ff.) and Barth (ibid. p. 205 f.) show by reference to the Syriac connective ''ai'' in the imperf. of the strong verb, is originally due to the analogy of verbs {{GHGheb|text=ל״י}} ({{GHGheb|text=מְחֵנִי}} = {{GHGheb|text=מְחֵינִי}} from ''m<sup>e</sup>ḥainî''), in which the final ''ê'' was used as a connecting vowel first of the imperat., then of the impf. (besides many forms with ''a'', {{GHGpar|60|d}}), and of the infin. and participle.</ref> ({{GHGheb|text=־ַ֫ נִי}}, {{GHGheb|text=־ֵ֫ נִי}}), used with verbal forms ending with a consonant (for exceptions, see {{GHGpar|59|g}} and {{GHGpar|60|e}}). This ''connecting vowel'' is ''a'' with the forms of the perfect, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=קְטָלַ֫נִי}}, {{GHGheb|text=קְטָלָ֫נוּ}}, {{GHGheb|text=קְטָלָם}} (on {{GHGheb|text=קְטָלֵךְ}}, the ordinary form of the 3rd masc. perf. with the 2nd fem. suffix, cf. below, g); and ''e'' (less frequently ''a'') with the forms of the imperfect and imperative, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=יִקְטְלֵ֫הוּ}}, {{GHGheb|text=קָטְלֵם}}; also with the infinitive and participles, when these do not take noun-suffixes (cf. {{GHGpar|61|a}} and h). The form {{GHGheb|text=וֹ}} also belongs to the suffixes of the perfect, since it has arisen from {{GHGheb|text=־ָ֫ הוּ}} (cf., however, {{GHGpar|60|d}}). With {{GHGheb|text=ךָ}}, {{GHGheb|text=כֶם}}, the connecting sound is only a vocal {{GHGterm|Š<sup>e</sup>wâ}}, which has arisen from an original short vowel, thus {{GHGheb|text=־ְךָ}}, {{GHGheb|text=־ְכֶם}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=קְטָֽלְךָ}} (''q<sup>e</sup>ṭāl<sup>e</sup>khā''), or when the final consonant of the verb is a guttural, {{GHGheb|text=־ֲךָ}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=שְׁלָֽחֲךָ}}. In {{GHGterm|pause}}, the original short vowel (''ă'') reappears as {{GHGterm|S<sup>e</sup>ghôl}} with the tone {{GHGheb|text=־ֶ֫ ךָ}} (also {{GHGheb|text=־ָ֫ ךְ}}, see g). On the appending of suffixes to the final {{GHGheb|text=וּן}} of the imperfect ({{GHGpar|47|m}}), see {{GHGpar|60|e}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|58|g}}
Rem. 1. As ''rare'' forms may be mentioned ''sing.'' 2nd pers. {{GHGterm|masc.}} {{GHGheb|text=־ְכָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=27|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=18|verse=44}}, &c., in {{GHGterm|pause}} also {{GHGheb|text=־ֶ֫ כָּה}} (see below, i); {{GHGterm|fem.}} {{GHGheb|text=כִי}}, {{GHGheb|text=־ֵ֫ כִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=103|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=137|verse=6|hidebook=1}}. Instead of the form {{GHGheb|text=־ֵךְ}}, which is usual even in the perfect (e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=4|verse=20}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=27|verse=26}}), {{GHGheb|text=־ָךְ}} occurs as {{GHGterm|fem.}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=60|verse=9}} (as {{GHGterm|masc.}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=6|verse=17}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=28|verse=45|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=30|verse=19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=55|verse=5|hidebook=1}} always in {{GHGterm|pause}}); with {{GHGterm|Munaḥ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=54|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=23|verse=37}}.—In the 3''rd masc.'' {{GHGheb|text=הֹ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=32|verse=25}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=23|verse=8}}; in the 3''rd fem.'' {{GHGheb|text=־ָה}} without {{GHGterm|Mappîq}} (cf. {{GHGpar|91|e}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=2|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=44|verse=19}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=1|verse=11}}, with<section end=par58 /><noinclude>
